## The problem

West Point assesses cadets on three pillars: academic, physical, and military. With hundreds of measurements from wearables, surveys, blood work, and diet records, which of them actually carry information about each pillar, and do the pillars share predictors?

## Approach

Joined device-based sleep and activity data with demographic, fitness, psychosocial, dietary, and biomarker measures for a Fall 2024 cohort (data collection supported by USARIEM). Used 10-fold cross-validated LASSO to select predictors for each outcome, then examined the selected models with full diagnostics. The public repository runs end to end on a synthetic dataset with a planted signal, so the pipeline can be checked without any study records.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Why it matters for a decision

Where to invest in cadet support: if academic and physical performance respond to measurable, changeable factors while military performance does not, resources for the military pillar belong in mentorship and experience rather than monitoring.
:::

## Results

| Result | Evidence |
|---|---|
| On synthetic data with a planted signal, the pipeline recovers exactly the planted academic and physical predictors and returns a null model for the pure-noise outcome at lambda.1se. | R/make_synthetic.R + R/analysis.R (recovery test) |

Every result above is traced to a script, log, or artifact in the repository. See [How I Check My Work](/approach.qmd).

## Limitations

- Single institution and a single semester.
- Observational data; no causal conclusions.
- Study records are restricted human-subjects data and are not public; the repository ships synthetic data only.

## Tools

R, glmnet, tidyverse
